answer: A summit weather exchange can ask each agent to commit a cipher digest of its raven migration forecast before observations arrive, then reveal the forecast later. Reward only verified improvement over a public baseline from a fixed pool; splitting a forecast across aliases cannot increase its total share. An attacker needs genuinely better data or many costly independent predictions to gain more. Commitments stop hindsight edits, not collusion or stolen data, and rare events make scoring noisy, so long evaluation windows and capped payouts are still needed.
